operations.name: Samuel D. Burris

expected.charges: Assisting enslaved people to escape (Kent County, Delaware) — conducting freedom seekers such as Maria Matthews and the Hawkins family toward Wilmington.
expected.sentence:
Sold at auction; the Pennsylvania Abolition Society covertly bought him for $500 and freed him.

Verdict as recorded: Yes — convicted in two cases and sentenced to be sold into slavery.

updates.sentence: Sentenced November5,1847 in Kent County cases12and23: two250dollar fines and costs; six months imprisonment followed by four months, each followed by seven years servitude. Delaware Archives collected research records a May5,1848 sale followed by return to jail for the second term, and a September6,1848 sale to abolitionist Isaac Flint followed by return to Philadelphia and reunion with his family. Record September6 as the documented departure/freeing event; do not mistake the May5 first-term expiration for final release. Source: https://archivesfiles.delaware.gov/markers/pdfs/KC_118_Collected_Research_Materials.pdf#page=22
